claim: Of the three reviewed topics, only fixed-point re-emission plausibly contributes to the allocation-dominated Cgen profile; armHints metadata and capture accounting cannot alone account for the 25->51.7 GiB RSS climb.
evidence: Perf finding knowledge-record:084b34f11911c8ac3bf8205c89b76fab: ~26% JSJIT, ~30% kernel anonymous page allocation/fault (clear_page_rep 8.27%), RSS 25->51.7 GiB over ~4.5 min, no source attribution; sample is one second of a different pinned build (2.0.25-f5185e38-pr967-pr968-e5c4efd-20261019, source 5df034e6). Topic 2 pass() re-emits the whole book per iteration and retains all C text/spins/maps; topic 1 reps reference book terms and add map/array/string metadata; topic 3 performs small per-call allocations and reduces code.
limits: Unverified correlation; the profile cannot name functions and may be dominated by other allocation sources (term caches, generated C strings, GC). A queue-gated measurement of pass count, per-pass byte totals and armHints size is needed.
